category: transactional email sender and SMTP relay

free_tier.stated: No permanent free tier. After an account is created and verified, a free trial gives Core plan access for one month, or a set amount of credits, with no credit card required. The Core plan allows 40,000 emails per month and costs USD 39.95 per month after the trial.
free_tier.notes: This is a one-month trial, not a continuing free tier. At the end of the trial the account loses platform access and can no longer send unless it upgrades to a paid plan. Public email accounts such as Gmail are not accepted at signup, so a work or private domain email is needed.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an outbound transactional sender

retention.stated: Free trial access lasts one month, after which platform access and sending stop without a paid upgrade. The exact reporting-history day windows are unverified: the first-party pricing page renders its feature table without day values.
retention.notes: The API docs state that returned data is limited to the Detailed Reporting History date range of the plan, but give no day counts. Day counts found on third-party pages were not used.

egress.terms: not applicable: an outbound email sender; volume is counted in emails sent, not in bytes transferred

interface_detail: The primary access path is SMTP relay on ports 25, 2525, 465 (SSL) and 587 (TLS), plus the HTTP Injection API. The schema has no SMTP interface term, so rest is used as the nearest term for the HTTP Injection API.
tooling: any SMTP client, the HTTP Injection API, or first-party SDKs in C#, PHP, Node.js, Python, Go, Java and Ruby
chaining: an outbound transactional sender with no inbound storage, used by an application that sends over SMTP or HTTP injection; the one-month trial window and the 40,000-email monthly Core allowance bound any sustained stack

limits.value: the free trial is one month of Core access; sending stops at the end of the trial without a paid plan
40,000 emails per month on the Core trial plan
the SocketLabs API is limited to 100 requests within 60 seconds; excess requests return an error; the /reports/message* endpoints are limited to 30 requests per 60 seconds

binding_note: The free access is one month, after which sending stops without a paid plan, so the trial window fails before the 40,000-email monthly allowance or the 100 requests per 60 seconds API rate is reached.

identity_cost.detail: The signup form asks for Full Name, Company Name and Company Email, asks the applicant to agree to the Terms of Service, and states 'Set up is fast, easy, and no credit card is required!'. It refuses public domains: 'Public accounts such as Gmail are not accepted'. Account creation passes a two-step review, with an automated analysis and then a human review; the approval guidance asks to 'Provide a valid phone number where you can be reached' and requires a publicly accessible business website. A phone number appears in the review guidance, but whether it is a mandatory form field is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: New accounts are throttled during an automatic warm-up period over the first weeks of service; by default a server that exceeds its monthly allowance by more than double is temporarily suspended.
confidence_note: Every number comes from first-party SocketLabs pages captured today: the signup form, the pricing FAQ, the API docs, the integration page and the help center. Delivery is not measured; no probe was run.

notes: SocketLabs has no permanent free tier. The only no-cost access is a one-month Core trial after account verification; public email domains are refused at signup and all new accounts pass a two-step review that may ask for a phone number.
